title: Per-atom latency signer and cache-penalty model for token cost attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, per-atom (subtoken/wordpiece) signing layer in the runtime traces and a small cache-penalty model to express how KV cache misses amplify per-token latency/cost. The goal is to produce high-cardinality but aggregated telemetry that lets SREs, runtime, and product teams answer: (1) how much of observed per-request latency comes from per-atom compute vs cache misses, (2) which model routes and sequence-length bands drive cache penalties, and (3) what per-token cost swing we should bill/charge back to customers in edge cases. This work touches tracing spans, metric emission, the log/metric pipeline schema, and dashboard panels for latency/error breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a stable span annotation: token.atom_index, token.type, kv_cache.hit:true|false, and token.step_duration_ms for each emission without >10% CPU overhead in p50 workloads
Collector/ingestion accepts new span tags and emits derived metrics: token_latency_ms.histogram, kv_miss_ratio by model/route, and cache_penalty_estimate.ms per-token
Dashboards updated: per-model and per-route panels showing per-atom p50/p95/p99, kv-miss contribution, and estimated per-token cost delta
End-to-end test showing attribution accuracy within +/-15% against offline ground-truth replay for a 10k-request synthetic workload
Feature gated rollout with an off-by-default runtime flag and no customer-facing API changes
notes: Design trade-off: emitting per-atom spans increases cardinality. We mitigate via aggregation at the tracer agent (rollup by model, route, sequence_length_bucket) and a 1-in-N sampling mode for full traces.
Cache-penalty model is intentionally simple: penalty_ms = base_miss_latency_ms * miss_factor(sequence_length_bucket, model_family) to keep downstream billing/audit explanation straightforward.
We will not expose per-customer raw atom traces externally; only aggregated metrics and audit-ready ledgers for customers with dedicated capacity and consent.
comments: 2026-02-19 — Aisha Patel: Spec draft posted to Confluence, requesting feedback from runtime and SRE. Key open Qs: sampling rate, tag naming, and the preferred histogram buckets for token latency.
2026-02-26 — Diego Ramirez: Implemented runtime span hooks and local test harness. Initial microbench shows +6% CPU and +8% mem for worst-case small-batch workloads. Will optimize serialization path.
2026-03-03 — Priya Nair (SRE): Asked to add a kv_cache.reason tag (e.g., cold_load|eviction|concurrency_block) to help root-cause; recommended keeping cold_load only for now to limit cardinality.
2026-03-06 — Code review (PR #1429): Requested better docs for sample-rate config and clearer naming: token.atom_index -> token.subtoken_index, token.step_duration_ms -> token.emit_duration_ms.

2026-03-09 — Diego Ramirez: Integrated collector-side aggregator to roll up per-atom metrics into token_latency_ms.histogram and kv_miss_ratio. End-to-end test harness ready; running long replay to validate accuracy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 — Spec + tracer hooks: finalize tag names, histogram buckets, and sampling strategy; implement lightweight runtime span annotations behind a feature flag.
Phase 2 — Collector aggregation: update trace collector to produce three derived metrics and a summarized kv-penalty estimate; add unit tests and replay-based validation.
Phase 3 — Dashboards and alerts: add panels for per-model/route token latency with kv-miss delta and create alerting rule for kv_miss_ratio > 5% sustained at p95
Phase 4 — Rollout: internal beta on dedicated capacity clusters, collect feedback, tune sampling; then enable opt-in for hosted customers and update billing ledgers for Dedicated customers.
Phase 5 — Post-launch: evaluate cost of high-cardinality telemetry and consider an explicit aggregation SDK to reduce payloads.
Fallbacks: if CPU/ingestion costs exceed threshold, switch to 1-in-50 sampling and increase rollup granularity by merging sequence_length buckets.
